title: DAWN: Diffusion-based Alignment and unfastening Workflow Network
authors: Hemant Kumar; Piyush Goenka; Nikhil Chopra
abstract: We present DAWN (Diffusion-based Alignment and unfastening Workflow Network), a hierarchical robotic framework designed to perform real-world, unfastening tasks through multi-modal sensory integration. Autonomous robotic unfastening is crucial for improving recycling processes, enhancing safety, and reducing operational costs; yet, it remains predominantly manual due to inherent challenges in precise screwdriver engagement with fasteners, detailed force execution, and robustness to environmental variability. title: BURGER: Benchmarking and Understanding Robotic Generalization via Embodied Drawing
authors: Xiangyu Xu; Bangshuai Peng; Ziyi Liu; Mengjie Zhao; Chenhao Lu; Zhengyang Fan
abstract: How effectively can vision-language-action (VLA) models learn diverse language-conditioned behaviors as training data scales? Investigating this question requires large and varied robot datasets, whose collection on physical robots remains costly. We introduce BURGER, a language-conditioned robotic drawing benchmark with a scalable, prompt-driven pipeline for generating continuous drawing trajectories, both in simulation and the real world. title: Quantize by Doing: Task-Guided Mixed-Precision Quantization of Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Jiuyi Xu; Xiao Hu; Meida Chen; Song Wang; Yang Ye; Yangming Shi
abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces the memory footprint of vision-language-action (VLA) models, but lowering bit widths while maintaining task performance remains challenging. Existing work has used sensitivity estimates from calibration data to assign bit widths to different model components. title: RoKON: Efficient and Adaptive Data-Enabled Predictive Control for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Akshun Sharma; Zhongqi Wei; Buqing Ou; Frederike Dümbgen
abstract: Data-enabled predictive control has recently emerged as a promising control paradigm, enabling a transparent optimal-control formulation without the need to learn an explicit dynamics model. This paper presents a number of extensions paving the path towards its use in real-time robotics tasks. title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
authors: Benjamin Pikus; Daniel Saunders; Mircea Mironenco; Salman Mohammadi; Mathew Mathew; Sirou Zhu
abstract: A robot policy needs to understand what a task is asking for in a scene, and how to move the robot to accomplish that task. authors: Yuanzhi He; Victor Romero-Cano; Jiayu Xu; Juan David Hernández; Gualtiero Colombo
abstract: Obstacle-aware robotic manipulation can require substantial interaction data when deep reinforcement learning policies are trained from scratch. authors: Tsung-Lung Yang
abstract: Robots that learn from people often see several valid ways to do the same task: pass an obstacle on the left or on the right, open the microwave or move the kettle first. A policy that re-decides at every step can waver between these ways mid-task. We ask when the action head (the part of a policy that turns the state into actions) matters, and how it should make this choice. authors: Jiabing Yang; Yuan Xu; Yixiang Chen; Qisen Ma; Peiyan Li; Kai Wang
abstract: Flow-matching Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generate expressive continuous trajectories for robotic manipulation, yet balancing real-time responsiveness with execution stability remains a persistent challenge. Standard deployment workflows typically treat numerical solver depth and execution horizon as decoupled choices. authors: Giorgia Pazzi; Giorgio Simonini; Michele Pierallini; Paolo Salaris; Giorgio Grioli; Manolo Garabini
abstract: Industries employ robots for repetitive tasks due to their high precision and performance, typically achieved through feedforward control actions based on an accurate robot description. However, an exact dynamic model can be difficult to obtain, especially for robots with elastic elements or when the payload changes. title: Flexible Language-Guided Representation Editing for Adaptive Robot Behavior
authors: Audrey Lee; Nathaniel Dennler; Ilia Sucholutsky; Andreea Bobu
abstract: Trajectory demonstrations show robots how to behave but not why, leaving them to guess which features of the task actually matter. Incorrect guesses produce misaligned internal representations and lead to incorrect robot behaviors. Because task features are often semantically defined, we argue that natural language is better suited for specifying features rather than relying on demonstrations. title: What Would Removing This Corruption Change? Failure Attribution for Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Carson Sobolewski; Anjali Parashar; Fei Chen; Yingke Li; Chuchu Fan
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are sensitive to visual corruptions, but knowing that a corruption is typically harmful does not establish whether removing it would benefit the current episode. Furthermore, when several corruptions co-occur, deciding what to correct requires understanding which ones contribute to failure risk and how much their removal would help. title: Robot Learning with Vision-Language-Action Models for Agricultural Manipulation
authors: Hamid Hafezi; Javad Mohammadpour Velni; Mohammadreza Davoodi
abstract: Robotic manipulation in agricultural environments remains challenging due to variations in plant geometry, occlusion, and camera viewpoints. Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) and generalist robot policies offer a promising approach to addressing these challenges by learning manipulation behaviors from multimodal observations and language instructions. authors: Zechen Wang; Zhenqi Qiu; Houlong Xiong; Suohang Zhang; Yiyu Ren; Wanting Xu
abstract: Human-collected robot manipulation data often mix successful behavior with retries, pauses, recoveries, and failures. Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning (AC-BC) can exploit such mixed-quality data, but only if the conditioning signal is both accurately constructed from offline trajectories and effectively incorporated into the policy's action-vector-field prediction. title: Learning to Compose: Recursive Self-Improvement of Shared Executable Stacks for Zero-Shot Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
authors: Yangzhi Chen; Feiran Liu; Zishuo Wang; Zijian Jin; Xin Zhu; Lecheng Ruan
abstract: Individually competent robot skills can fail when composed: tools may lack a required capability, completion signals may misrepresent physical progress, and one skill may leave a state that violates its successor's prerequisites. We introduce Recursia, a recursive self-improvement framework that treats the shared executable stack, rather than individual task programs, as the persistent unit of improvement. authors: Mateusz Jaszczuk; Paris Perdikaris; Nadia Figueroa
abstract: With advancements in learning-based policies, robots are increasingly being deployed in human-centric environments, such as manufacturing floors and homes, where safe and precise operation requires compensating for unknown loads while remaining compliant during human interactions. title: Embodiment-Aware Planning for Heterogeneous Bimanual Manipulation
authors: Sukhvansh Jain; Anurag Maurya; Shivam Vats; Narendra Kumar Dhar; Ravi Prakash
abstract: Many manipulation tasks that are effortless for dexterous human hands remain challenging for robotic systems equipped with simple, task-specialized grippers. Industrial platforms commonly rely on end-effectors such as suction cups or parallel-jaw grippers, yet no single mode can reliably satisfy the diverse constraints encountered across different phases of complex manipulation tasks, including pickup, reorientation, insertion, and constrained placement. title: TS-WAM: Temporal Latent Actions and World-Action Coupling for Vision-Language Robot Control
authors: Menghao Yin; Jiaju Yin; Xiyue Dong; Lixin Xu; Zhenhui Zhang; Ke Zhang
abstract: Many vision-language-action policies rely on action-labeled robot demonstrations and lack an explicit mechanism for predicting future visual states. These limitations hinder learning from action-free videos and can encourage overfitting to demonstration conditions, weakening generalization and robustness. title: Sub-Millisecond Reflexes for Continuous Physical Human-Robot Interaction
authors: Jon Škerlj; Sami Haddadin
abstract: Continuous physical human-robot interaction requires robots to rapidly adapt their control behaviour without interrupting task execution. However, existing ROS 2 control architectures rely on stop-to-switch mechanisms that introduce substantial delays and interrupt execution. authors: Jiuyi Xu; Chengyuan Qian; Zhengzhong Tu; Yang Sui; Yangming Shi
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models present a promising paradigm for general-purpose robot manipulation, but closed-loop deployment is often limited by inference efficiency: at each timestep, high-resolution, often multi-view images are encoded into hundreds of visual tokens that dominate transformer computation and latency. authors: Manav Kulshrestha; Apoorva Vashisth; Damon Conover; Aniket Bera
abstract: Task-Oriented Grasping (TOG) has emerged as an important skill for purposeful robotic manipulation. Given the task of using a knife to "slice bread," a robot must choose to grasp from the handle, whereas for "hand[ing] the knife over," it is preferable for the handle to remain unobstructed for safe handoff. authors: Colton Crosby; Hao Wang; Mac Schwager; Somil Bansal
abstract: State-of-the-art visuomotor policies are increasingly capable of executing complex tasks, yet can fail during deployment in ways they cannot predict or recover from on their own. Improving their performance and robustness typically requires collecting more data, retraining, or modifying the policy architecture, all of which are time- and resource-intensive in practice. authors: Maria Attarian; Yifan Ruan; Claas Voelcker; Chenyang Cao; Amy Zhang; Peter Stone
abstract: While Vision-Language-Action models have enabled impressive cross-task transfer in zero-shot settings, \emph{adaptation} methods are often necessary to achieve consistent performance on novel tasks. However, even though a wealth of methods for adaptation have been proposed, it is unclear how to choose the best method based on available trajectories. title: ReTrace: Cross-Stage Failure Attribution for Self-Improving Robotic Manipulation
authors: Yue Yu; Bin Zhu; Junhui Li; Jiayu Wang; Shijie Zhou; Jingjing Chen
abstract: General-purpose multimodal foundation models are increasingly capable of directly controlling robots, yet improving their manipulation capabilities through autonomous interaction remains challenging. A key challenge to such self-improvement is learning from failures in complex manipulation tasks involving cross-stage dependencies, where an action may succeed locally but cause a later stage to fail. title: Scaling Latent Motor Adaptation to Coordinated Bimanual Manipulation
authors: Seung-Bin Joo; Alessandro Albini; Luca Wiehe; Perla Maiolino; Daniel Olmeda Reino; João F. Henriques
abstract: Robust manipulation under uncertain object dynamics and geometry remains a core challenge in real-world robotics. Policies trained under fixed assumptions often degrade when object mass, friction, scale, or shape vary. Embedding-based adaptation methods such as Rapid Motor Adaptation (RMA) address this by conditioning actions on latent representations of environment dynamics inferred from interaction history. authors: Bahey Tharwat; Iman Nematollahi; Marvin Alles; Xingyuan Zhang; Akshay L Chandra; Abhinav Valada
abstract: Generalist robot policies are trained with imitation learning and are bounded by the quality and coverage of their demonstrations. Reinforcement learning can improve and extend them, either by fine-tuning the policy weights or by training a small module to steer the input noise of a frozen generative policy. authors: Mohammad Khoshnazar; Mohammad Dehghani Tezerjani; Zhiyuan Gao; Deyuan Qu; Max Gandyra; Yanxiang Zhan
abstract: A generated video of a task the robot is about to perform is useful guidance only if it depicts the phase the robot is actually in. title: Embodied Zero-Shot Task Planning via Hardware-Aware LLM-VLM Integration for Grounded Robotic Manipulation
authors: Lonnie Tankersley; Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz; Soroush Korivand
abstract: Large language models can translate natural-language instructions into plausible manipulation plans, but robotic execution requires physically grounded decisions that respect robot embodiment, workspace geometry, reachability, collision constraints, and grasp feasibility. This paper presents a hardware-aware large language model-vision-language model (LLM-VLM) manipulation framework for a simulated Franka Research 3 robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. title: Control-Ready Uncertainty for Trajectory Diffusion
authors: Zhiwei Xue; Jia Yue Kam; Jinhang Qiu; Yifeng Cheng; Ege Gursoy; Jiaming Wang
abstract: Diffusion models can represent complex, multimodal trajectory distributions, but extracting uncertainty from them typically requires costly Monte Carlo sampling. This limits their use in real-time control, where robots must rapidly assess risk and maintain safety margins. authors: Mohammad Khoshnazar; Mohammad Dehghani Tezerjani; Deyuan Qu; Zhiyuan Gao; Yanxiang Zhan; Jeroen Schafer
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies assume the embodiment on which they were trained and can fail when a joint fault changes how commanded actions are physically executed. Existing fault-recovery methods often require task-specific retraining, fault labels, explicit diagnosis, or privileged embodiment information. authors: Chen Cai; Steven Liu
abstract: Close-proximity multi-arm manipulation requires collision models that are both geometrically accurate and differentiable enough for real-time optimization. Classical geometry checkers provide reliable distances but are difficult to use inside gradient-based model predictive control, while conservative proxy models can restrict tightly coupled motion. authors: Tzu-Yu Chuang; Ching-Hsiang Chang; Yi-Hsiu Lee; Yi-Ting Chen; Min Sun; YuanFu Yang
abstract: Generative world models provide rich predictions of how manipulation scenes may evolve toward task objectives, yet those futures do not directly expose the compact task variables required by control. When training supervises future prediction alone, terminal goal accuracy is not an explicit learning objective, even when geometric recovery is available. authors: Pranav Wagh; Yu Fang; Yue Yang; Mingyu Ding
abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation is often built by chaining independently trained skills. Although each skill can be reliable in isolation, performance degrades sharply when skills are chained: each downstream skill must start from the state its predecessor leaves behind rather than from its training distribution. authors: Yuan Xu; Yixiang Chen; Qisen Ma; Jiabing Yang; Peiyan Li; Kai Wang
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have become a central paradigm for robot policy learning, which predict actions in three forms: raw action chunks, discrete action tokens, or continuous action latents. However, existing action representations primarily model action trajectories, with limited consideration of the visual dynamics induced by these actions. abstract: Pose error in precision assembly can corrupt not only what a robot observes but also the coordinate frame in which it acts. authors: Junwon Seo; Andrea Bajcsy
abstract: In this paper, we study robust decision-making in the latent space of world models (WMs). authors: Kuan-Hsun Tu; Hsuan-Chi Liu; Jia-Wei Liao; Chien-Sheng Chiang; Cheng-Fu Chou; Tsung-Wei Ke
abstract: We introduce CNP-Flow, a flow matching framework for temporal generation that learns conditional source distributions through flow reversal. authors: Seongheon Park; Heecheol Kim; Shulin Tian; Lilika Makabe; Namiko Saito; Katsushi Ikeuchi
abstract: Scaling robot data and model capacity has improved Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, but further progress is constrained by the high cost of robotic data. Verifier-guided test-time scaling offers an efficient alternative by sampling multiple action candidates and selecting the one most likely to lead to task success at inference time. authors: Elizabeth Peiros; Derek Chen; Lucas Yager; Edward Lee; Kevin Wang; Zoe Samuels
abstract: Improvements in human-robot physical interaction (pHRI) can have major implications for physical therapy, search and rescue, and telemedicine. authors: Chunyu Jiang; Yichen Cai; Shuai Li; Wenbin Sun; João Carvalho; Kostas Daniilidis
abstract: Contact-rich manipulation requires a robot to be precise in free space to establish the intended contacts, and compliant once in contact to avoid excessive forces. authors: Xinjie Liu; Ruihan Zhao; Anirban Chaudhuri; Cyrus Neary; Ufuk Topcu; David Fridovich-Keil
abstract: Policy gradient methods for on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) can become unstable when expensive, scarce target-domain data yield noisy gradient estimates. authors: Junyi Hu; Zhewen He; Zhenhua Li; Yi Fang

authors: Zhugang Liu; Kaichuang Zhang; Jinman Zhang; Pu Sun; Martha Asare; Jose Hernandez
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models unify visual perception, language understanding, and action generation, offering new opportunities for automation in additive manufacturing (AM). authors: Jiajun Liu; Yifan Chen; Yichao Liu; Jiayi Zhang; Ruoqu Chen; Shaoxuan Xie
abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation reuses skills across many task compositions, but improving these compositions with additional end-to-end demonstrations is costly. authors: Seungeun Rho; Jeonghwan Kim; Xue Bin Peng; Sehoon Ha

authors: Rho Team; Simran Bagaria; Daphne Chen; Dean Fortier; Jianlong Fu; Michael Harrison

abstract: A robot working alongside people must reason about what they have done, in what order, and with what intent. authors: Haoran Zhang; Yifu Lu; Boyang Wang; Xuhui Kang; Yen-Ling Kuo; Zezhou Cheng

abstract: Single-view mesh reconstruction predicts object meshes and spatial layouts from a single observation, making it attractive for fast robot spatial reasoning and real-to-sim digital twins. abstract: Functional robotic grasping requires a policy that generalizes across diverse object geometries and poses while maintaining task-specific contact precision. authors: Yueci Deng

authors: Litian Liang; Jingxi Xu; Xinda Qi; Yujun Cai; Houzhu Ding; Luqi Wang

authors: Namai Chandra; Shriram Damodaran; Lin Wang
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel at mapping visual inputs and natural language instructions directly to robotic control policies. authors: Tobias Jülg; Seongjin Bien; Simon Hilber; Yannik Blei; Pierre Krack; Maximilian Li

authors: David Young; Swan Yi Htet
abstract: Modular neural network pipelines suffer from error compounding: noise at any module boundary propagates and potentially amplifies through subsequent modules. authors: Wenlong Huang; Yu-Wei Chao; Arsalan Mousavian; Ming-Yu Liu; Dieter Fox; Kaichun Mo

abstract: Koopman operator theory has emerged as a leading data-driven approach that relies on a judicious choice of observable functions to realize global linear representations of nonlinear systems in the lifted observable space. abstract: Modeling dexterous hand-object interactions is challenging as it requires understanding how subtle finger motions influence the environment through contact with objects. authors: Abdullah Tokmak; Thomas B. Schön; Dominik Baumann
abstract: Safe Bayesian optimization (BO) with Gaussian processes is an effective tool for tuning control policies in safety-critical real-world systems, specifically due to its sample efficiency and safety guarantees. abstract: We study data-driven identification of interpretable hybrid robot dynamics, where an analytical rigid-body dynamics model is complemented by a learned residual torque term. abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit strong priors from pretrained Vision-Language Models (VLMs), but naive fine-tuning often disrupts these representations and harms generalization. authors: Maria Ibrahim; Alap Kshirsagar; Dorothea Koert; Jan Peters

abstract: Humans can learn a new manipulation task from one or two demonstrations and then perform it in a new room, with new objects, under new constraints. abstract: Generative models have shown great promise as trajectory planners, given their affinity to modeling complex distributions and guidable inference process. Previous works have successfully applied these in the context of robotic manipulation but perform poorly when the required solution does not exist as a complete trajectory within the training set. authors: Caleb Chuck; Fan Feng; Carl Qi; Chang Shi; Siddhant Agarwal; Amy Zhang
abstract: Hindsight relabeling is a powerful tool for overcoming sparsity in goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL), especially in certain domains such as navigation and locomotion. authors: Junwon Seo; Kensuke Nakamura; Andrea Bajcsy
abstract: Recent advances in generative world models have enabled classical safe control methods, such as Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability, to generalize to complex robotic systems operating directly from high-dimensional sensor observations. title: TeLoGraF: Temporal Logic Planning via Graph-encoded Flow Matching
authors: Yue Meng; Chuchu Fan
abstract: Learning to solve complex tasks with signal temporal logic (STL) specifications is crucial to many real-world applications. authors: Minseok Song; JeongHo Ha; Bonggyeong Park; Daehyung Park
abstract: We aim to solve the problem of manipulating deformable objects, particularly elastic bands, in real-world scenarios. authors: Leihui Li; Lixuepiao Wan; Volker Krueger; Xuping Zhang
abstract: Hand-eye calibration is a common problem in the field of collaborative robotics, involving the determination of the transformation matrix between the visual sensor and the robot flange to enable vision-based robotic tasks. authors: Simon Manschitz; Berk Gueler; Wei Ma; Dirk Ruiken
abstract: Shared autonomy allows for combining the global planning capabilities of a human operator with the strengths of a robot such as repeatability and accurate control. In a real-time teleoperation setting, one possibility for shared autonomy is to let the human operator decide for the rough movement and to let the robot do fine adjustments, e.g., when the view of the operator is occluded. authors: Max Muchen Sun; Allison Pinosky; Todd Murphey
abstract: Ergodic coverage effectively generates exploratory behaviors for embodied agents by aligning the spatial distribution of the agent's trajectory with a target distribution, where the difference between these two distributions is measured by the ergodic metric. However, existing ergodic coverage methods are constrained by the limited set of ergodic metrics available for control synthesis, fundamentally limiting their performance. authors: Rongtao Xu; Jian Zhang; Minghao Guo; Youpeng Wen; Haoting Yang; Min Lin
abstract: Robotic manipulation faces critical challenges in understanding spatial affordances--the "where" and "how" of object interactions--essential for complex manipulation tasks like wiping a board or stacking objects. Existing methods, including modular-based and end-to-end approaches, often lack robust spatial reasoning capabilities. title: A ROS2-based software library for inverse dynamics computation
authors: Vincenzo Petrone; Enrico Ferrentino; Pasquale Chiacchio
abstract: Inverse dynamics computation is a critical component in robot control, planning and simulation, enabling the calculation of joint torques required to achieve a desired motion. This paper presents a ROS2-based software library designed to solve the inverse dynamics problem for robotic systems. The library is built around an abstract class with three concrete implementations: one for simulated robots and two for real UR10 and Franka robots. authors: Yuan Meng; Xiangtong Yao; Haihui Ye; Yirui Zhou; Shengqiang Zhang; Zhenguo Sun
abstract: Robotic long-horizon manipulation requires robots to compose perception, reasoning, and action over extended task sequences, yet existing language-conditioned frameworks often rely on dense step-wise feedback, learned action policies, or unstructured prompting, which limits robustness and generalization. authors: Yuan Meng; Xiangtong Yao; Yansong Wu; Liding Zhang; Yixiao Nie; Zhenshan Bing
abstract: Long-horizon manipulation under sparse rewards remains challenging for reinforcement learning due to delayed feedback and inefficient exploration. Existing skill-based approaches often assume a fixed parametric prior (e.g., a single Gaussian), limiting their ability to capture diverse and multi-modal skill structures required for complex tasks. authors: Patrizio Perugini; Jens Lundell; Katharina Friedl; Danica Kragic
abstract: We address prehensile pushing, the problem of manipulating a grasped object by pushing against the environment. authors: Ali Parsaee; Fahim Shahriar; Chuxin He; Ruiqing Tan
abstract: In recent times, reinforcement learning (RL) with physical robots has attracted the attention of a wide range of researchers. authors: Giovanni Franzese; Max Spahn; Jens Kober; Cosimo Della Santina
abstract: To increase the reliability of collaborative robots in performing daily tasks, we require them to be accurate and not only repeatable. However, having a calibrated kinematics model is regrettably a luxury, as available calibration tools are usually more expensive than the robots themselves. authors: Yu Fang; Yue Yang; Xinghao Zhu; Kaiyuan Zheng; Gedas Bertasius; Daniel Szafir
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models present a promising paradigm by training policies directly on real robot datasets like Open X-Embodiment. However, the high cost of real-world data collection hinders further data scaling, thereby restricting the generalizability of VLAs. title: RISE: Robust Imitation through Stochastic Encoding
authors: Mumuksh Tayal; Manan Tayal; Ravi Prakash
abstract: Ensuring safety in robotic systems remains a fundamental challenge, especially when deploying offline policy-learning methods such as imitation learning in dynamic environments. authors: Ali Umut Kaypak; Shiqing Wei; Prashanth Krishnamurthy; Farshad Khorrami
abstract: Inter-robot collisions pose a significant safety risk when multiple robotic arms operate in close proximity. authors: Hossein Karami; Antony Thomas; Fulvio Mastrogiovanni
abstract: In this paper, we present an approach for integrated task and motion planning based on an AND/OR graph network, which is used to represent task-level states and actions, and we leverage it to implement different classes of task and motion planning problems (TAMP). authors: Chih H. Huang; Pranav Jadhav; Brian Plancher; Zachary Kingston
abstract: Sampling-based motion planning algorithms, like the Rapidly-Exploring Random Tree (RRT) and its widely used variant, RRT-Connect, provide efficient solutions for high-dimensional planning problems faced by real-world robots. authors: Marco Iannotta; Johannes A. Stork; Erik Schaffernicht; Todor Stoyanov
abstract: With the rising demand for flexible manufacturing, robots are increasingly expected to operate in dynamic environments where local -- such as slight offsets or size differences in workpieces -- are common. authors: Pablo C. Lopez-Custodio; Yuhe Gong; Luis F. C. Figueredo
abstract: Modern robotics applications require an inverse kinematics (IK) solver that is fast, robust and consistent, and that provides all possible solutions. authors: Yufei Wang; Ziyu Wang; Mino Nakura; Pratik Bhowal; Chia-Liang Kuo; Yi-Ting Chen
abstract: This paper presents ArticuBot, in which a single learned policy enables a robotics system to open diverse categories of unseen articulated objects in the real world. authors: Xiangtong Yao; Yirui Zhou; Yuan Meng; Liangyu Dong; Lin Hong; Zitao Zhang
abstract: Current robotic pick-and-place policies typically require consistent gripper configurations across training and inference. authors: Joey Hejna; Suvir Mirchandani; Ashwin Balakrishna; Annie Xie; Ayzaan Wahid; Jonathan Tompson
abstract: The performance of imitation learning policies often hinges on the datasets with which they are trained. authors: Kensuke Nakamura; Lasse Peters; Andrea Bajcsy
abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability is a rigorous mathematical framework that enables robots to simultaneously detect unsafe states and generate actions that prevent future failures. authors: Xuancun Lu; Zhengxian Huang; Xinfeng Li; Chi Zhang; Xiaoyu Ji; Wenyuan Xu
abstract: LLM-based robots use Large Language Models (LLMs) as planners to translate natural language instructions into policies such as grasp(), move_to(), and open_gripper(). abstract: A world model provides an agent with a representation of its environment, enabling it to predict the causal consequences of its actions. abstract: In this paper, we introduce RoboMIND (Multi-embodiment Intelligence Normative Data for Robot Manipulation), a dataset containing 107k demonstration trajectories across 479 diverse tasks involving 96 object classes. authors: Ran Tian; Yilin Wu; Chenfeng Xu; Masayoshi Tomizuka; Jitendra Malik; Andrea Bajcsy
abstract: Visuomotor robot policies, increasingly pre-trained on large-scale datasets, promise significant advancements across robotics domains. authors: Carson Kohlbrenner; Caleb Escobedo; S. Sandra Bae; Alexander Dickhans; Alessandro Roncone
abstract: Developing whole-body tactile skins for robots remains a challenging task, as existing solutions often prioritize modular, one-size-fits-all designs, which, while versatile, fail to account for the robot's specific shape and the unique demands of its operational context. authors: Aurel X. Appius; Emiland Garrabe; Francois Helenon; Mahdi Khoramshahi; Mohamed Chetouani; Stephane Doncieux

authors: Shutong Chen; Emmanouil Spyrakos-Papastavridis; Yichao Jin; Yansha Deng

authors: Federico Califano; Daniel Logmans; Wesley Roozing

authors: Daehee Lee; Minjong Yoo; Woo Kyung Kim; Wonje Choi; Honguk Woo
abstract: Continual Imitation Learning (CiL) involves extracting and accumulating task knowledge from demonstrations across multiple stages and tasks to achieve a multi-task policy. authors: Zhendong Wang; Zhaoshuo Li; Ajay Mandlekar; Zhenjia Xu; Jiaojiao Fan; Yashraj Narang

authors: Michiel Nikken; Nicolò Botteghi; Wesley Roozing; Federico Califano

abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has the potential to enable robots to learn from their own actions in the real world. abstract: Collaborative robots are increasingly deployed alongside humans in factories, hospitals, schools, and other domains to enhance teamwork and efficiency. abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) in robotics faces significant hurdles regarding sample efficiency and generalization across varying goals. abstract: Anomaly detection is essential for robotic perception and industrial inspection, yet most benchmarks are collected under controlled conditions with fixed viewpoints and stable illumination. abstract: Motion planning for articulated robots has traditionally been governed by algorithms that operate within manufacturer-defined payload limits. authors: Hyun Joe Jeong; Rosy Chen; Andrea Bajcsy

authors: Mazeyu Ji; Ri-Zhao Qiu; Xueyan Zou; Xiaolong Wang
abstract: The ability for robots to perform efficient and zero-shot grasping of object parts is crucial for practical applications and is becoming prevalent with recent advances in Vision-Language Models (VLMs). authors: Lingyun Chen; Haoyu Yu; Abdeldjallil Naceri; Abdalla Swikir; Sami Haddadin
abstract: Non-prehensile object transportation offers a way to enhance robotic performance in object manipulation tasks, especially with unstable objects. authors: Li-Heng Lin; Yuchen Cui; Amber Xie; Tianyu Hua; Dorsa Sadigh
abstract: Few-shot imitation learning relies on only a small amount of task-specific demonstrations to efficiently adapt a policy for a given downstream tasks. authors: Kübra Karacan; Anran Zhang; Hamid Sadeghian; Fan Wu; Sami Haddadin
abstract: Despite recent advancements in torque-controlled tactile robots, integrating them into manufacturing settings remains challenging, particularly in complex environments. authors: Donghoon Kim; Minjong Yoo; Honguk Woo
abstract: Goal-conditioned (GC) policy learning often faces a challenge arising from the sparsity of rewards, when confronting long-horizon goals. abstract: In safety-critical robot planning or control, manually specifying safety constraints or learning them from demonstrations can be challenging. abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms can learn robotic control tasks from visual observations, but they often require a large amount of data, especially when the visual scene is complex and unstructured. authors: Matthias Mayr; Julian M. Salt-Ducaju
abstract: Cartesian impedance control is a type of motion control strategy for robots that improves safety in partially unknown environments by achieving a compliant behavior of the robot with respect to its external forces. This compliant robot behavior has the added benefit of allowing physical human guidance of the robot. authors: Tobias Löw; Sylvain Calinon

abstract: This paper is about fast slosh free fluid transportation. Existing approaches are either computationally heavy or only suitable for specific robots and container shapes. authors: Sebastian Wallkotter; Mohamed Chetouani; Ginevra Castellano

abstract: We aim to teach robots to perform simple object manipulation tasks by watching a single video demonstration. abstract: Robotic manipulation of cloth has applications ranging from fabrics manufacturing to handling blankets and laundry. abstract: In this paper, we present a framework that unites obstacle avoidance and deliberate physical interaction for robotic manipulators. abstract: Grasp synthesis for 3D deformable objects remains a little-explored topic, most works aiming to minimize deformations. abstract: We study the problem of learning a range of vision-based manipulation tasks from a large offline dataset of robot interaction. abstract: Robotic manipulation of cloth remains challenging for robotics due to the complex dynamics of the cloth, lack of a low-dimensional state representation, and self-occlusions. abstract: While there exists many methods for manipulating rigid objects with parallel-jaw grippers, grasping with multi-finger robotic hands remains a quite unexplored research topic. abstract: Learning-based approaches for robotic grasping using visual sensors typically require collecting a large size dataset, either manually labeled or by many trial and errors of a robotic manipulator in the real or simulated world. We propose a simpler learning-from-demonstration approach that is able to detect the object to grasp from merely a single demonstration using a convolutional neural network we call GraspNet. In order to increase robustness and decrease the training time even further, we leverage data from previous demonstrations to quickly fine-tune a GrapNet for each new demonstration.
